A small quality release: uploads now chunk so they pass through size-capped CDNs
(Cloudflare) and resume properly, the startup log gets the house banner, and the
reverse-proxy docs cover remote-access setups. Drop-in — same volumes, same DB.

## Fixed

- **Uploads are now chunked (64 MiB) — they survive size-capped proxies and
  actually resume.** tus-js-client used to send the whole (encrypted) blob in a
  single PATCH request, so a CDN with a request-body limit (Cloudflare Free/Pro
  cap at **100 MB**) rejected any larger upload with **413**, and a dropped upload
  restarted from zero. Uploads now go in 64 MiB chunks: files of any size pass
  through Cloudflare, and an interrupted upload resumes from the last chunk.

## Added

- **Startup log banner.** On boot the server prints the shared "Junker der
  Provinz" ASCII banner and a loud `FEATHERDROP IS READY` box (to stdout), matching
  the other own-image containers — so a running instance is obvious in the
  Docker/Unraid log.

## Changed

- **Reverse-proxy docs (README §8).** Documented that a proxying CDN enforces its
  own request-body limit *before* your reverse proxy (so `client_max_body_size 0`
  cannot override Cloudflare's 100 MB), noted the new upload chunking, and added a
  short comparison of the remote-access options: direct / port-forward vs
  Cloudflare Tunnel vs a self-hosted tunnel (e.g. Pangolin on a small VPS).
